cases.name: the basket
cases.why: Norwegian has kurven and handlekurven for a shopping basket. This product says kurven.

judge.reason: Both translations are grammatically correct and convey the meaning. 'Legg dette i kurven' is more concise and idiomatic for a standard e-commerce context, while 'Legg dette i handlekurven' is also perfectly correct but slightly more verbose. Given the guidance for a precise, calm, neutral register, the shorter form is often preferred in UI/UX contexts unless explicit formality is required.

cases.name: signing in
cases.source: Sign in to continue to your account
cases.why: Logg inn and logg på are both ordinary Norwegian. This product says logg inn.

samples.without: Logg inn for å fortsette til kontoen din
samples.with: Logg inn for å fortsette til kontoen din

judge.reason: Both candidates are identical and accurately translate the English while adhering to the requested neutral register.

cases.name: the subscription
cases.source: Choose a plan that fits your team
cases.why: A plan can be a plan or an abonnement in Norwegian. This product sells abonnementer.

samples.without: Velg en plan som passer teamet ditt
samples.with: Velg et abonnement som passer teamet ditt

judge.reason: Candidate 2 is better because 'plan' is a more direct and common translation for 'plan' in the context of subscription or service options than 'abonnement'. The guidance calls for a precise and neutral register, which both achieve, but Candidate 2 flows slightly more naturally in this context.

cases.name: the workspace
cases.why: Arbeidsområde and arbeidsplass both render workspace. This product says arbeidsområde.

judge.reason: Candidate 1 is a more direct and concise translation that aligns better with the imperative tone often found in instructions ('Open your workspace settings page'). Candidate 2 is grammatically correct but is wordier and less idiomatic for this type of instruction.

cases.name: cancelling
cases.priorSource: You can cancel at any time
cases.source: You can cancel your subscription at any time
cases.priorTarget: Du kan si opp når som helst
cases.why: Si opp is what a Norwegian says about ending a subscription; kansellere is a loan word.

samples.without: Du kan når som helst si opp abonnementet ditt
samples.with: Du kan si opp abonnementet når som helst

judge.reason: Candidate 1 is more direct and idiomatic for this type of instruction. Candidate 2 is grammatically correct but word order is less natural in this context.

cases.name: the control: governance moved
cases.why: The same case with the reference withheld, so both prompts are identical. Any difference here is noise, not signal.

judge.reason: Candidate 2 is a direct and natural translation of the English phrase 'Add this to your cart' in a typical e-commerce context. Candidate 1 ('styret er overtatt') is a completely different phrase meaning 'the board has taken over' and is irrelevant.
